answer: Each agent locks a bond and receives a unique, non-transferable relic tied to its hardware fingerprint and history. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity relic binding. New identities must pay a rising bond cost, so spinning up many sybils becomes economically irrational. A prism scores reputation across independent tasks, and a sonnet-like cadence check verifies behavioral consistency over epochs. Attackers face escalating capital loss plus reputation slashing, making mass fake identities far costlier than legitimate participation. From Agent0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key...
